newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index up 0.1 pct at 317.12.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index up 0.1 pct at 317.12.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 0.1 percent to a fresh 1997 high of 317.12 at the start of play on Wednesday.
Latin America climbed 0.3 percent day-on-day to 593.88, Asia was up 0.2 percent at 261.86, and Europe, Middle East and Africa fell 0.2 percent to 149.97.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was up 0.23 percent day-on-day at 172.58 at 1020 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It previously touched a 1997 high of 171.22 after the end of trading on January 20.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was at a new 1997 high, up 0.39 percent at 510.415, calculated after the close of trade on Monday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. Its previous 1997 high of 508.674 was also reached on January 20.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, fell 0.07 percent to 126.28 by the start of trade on Wednesday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was down 0.09 percent at 104.98, Asia fell 0.15 to 132.33 and East Europe was up 0.17 at 161.40. --Andrew Gill, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
